headline_seed: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña impeached and arrested - BBC

consensus_facts: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña was impeached and removed from office on Friday by the Senate and placed under house arrest.
The crisis was triggered by the collapse of Ueno Bank, a major digital bank seized by Paraguay's central bank earlier in the week.
Ueno Bank had roughly 3 million customers, a large share of Paraguay's adult population, who lost access to their savings and bank cards.
Peña, a former IMF economist, had held a stake in the parent/holding company linked to Ueno Bank until last year (March 2025 per Al Jazeera).
Peña appointed a former Ueno-connected executive, Carlos Carvallo, to head the central bank; Carvallo has since resigned.
Vice-President Pedro Alliana, a member of the conservative Colorado Party, was sworn in as interim president and will serve until August 2028.

Impeachment charges centered on conflicts of interest, influence over regulators, and the diversion/deposit of public pension funds into Ueno (BBC and Hindustan Times cite the pension fund figure; Hindustan Times and Al Jazeera cite the $355m/$380m pension deposit).
Peña offered to resign/step down before the vote but senators proceeded with impeachment; he denied any wrongdoing.
Prosecutors ordered Peña to remain under house arrest pending questioning by anti-corruption/economic crimes authorities.
The central bank said deposits were insured up to roughly $36,000-$37,000, covering nearly all customers.

positions.BBC News: Impeachment passed 44 of 45 senators in favour, with one lawmaker absent.
positions.Hindustan Times: All 44 senators present voted in favour of removal (frames it as all present voting yes rather than 44 of 45).

disagreements.topic: Pension fund amount deposited at Ueno

positions.Al Jazeera English: About $380m invested by Paraguay's state pension and health fund (of $800m public funds managed).
positions.Hindustan Times: The state pension fund deposited $355 million, allegedly exceeding legal limits.

disagreements.topic: Date the central bank seized the bank

positions.Al Jazeera English: Central bank put Ueno into resolution on Monday.
positions.Hindustan Times: Financial regulators seized Ueno Bank on Tuesday.

positions.Al Jazeera English: Fund insures up to about $36,000 per customer, covering ~97 percent of customers.
positions.Hindustan Times: Deposits insured up to approximately $37,000, covering nearly all Ueno customers.
Prosecutors charged 27 people including controlling shareholder Miguel Vázquez; six bank directors in pretrial detention; arrest of ex-central bank chief Carvallo ordered; luxury assets seized.
positions.BBC News: Does not report the 27 charges or asset seizures; focuses on Peña's impeachment and upcoming questioning.
positions.Al Jazeera English: Notes only that the Public Prosecutor's office ordered multiple criminal investigations, without the 27-person figure.

framing_analysis.Reuters: Headline-only in this dossier (no retrievable body text). Headline frames the event as 'ex-president Peña placed under house arrest after impeachment' — emphasizes the arrest consequence, labels him 'ex-president.' No body-level detail available to assess.
framing_analysis.BBC News: Two identical full-text entries (Articles 2 and 3). Leads with 'late night political drama,' framing it as a dramatic democratic moment. Emphasizes the unanimous cross-party vote (even his own party), the stripping of immunity, and the human scale ('more than half of Paraguay's population without access to their savings'). Includes Peña's apology and defence lawyer's 'reckless accusation' rebuttal for balance. Quotes Senator Filizzola calling it 'the biggest corruption scandal in our democratic history.' Lighter on the banking mechanics and parallel prosecutions.
framing_analysis.Al Jazeera English: An explainer/deep-dive format focused on the banking system and systemic context ('only its latest banking crisis'). Leads with the economic mechanics — solvency ratios, insider lending, $146m in loans to owner-linked firms. Foregrounds protester voices and anti-Colorado-Party sentiment ('70 years of plunder'), giving the story a populist/accountability frame. Strongest on how the bank failed and least focused on the courtroom/impeachment procedure.
framing_analysis.The Times of India: Headline-only in this dossier (no retrievable body text). Headline frames it as the Senate 'ousting' the former president and prosecutors placing him under house arrest — dual emphasis on legislative removal and prosecutorial action. No body to assess.
framing_analysis.Hindustan Times: Full-text and the most procedurally detailed. Leads with the succession angle — Pedro Alliana sworn in — then the impeachment and arrest. Strongest on the parallel criminal investigation (27 charged, Vázquez named, pretrial detentions, asset seizures) and on scrutiny of Alliana himself. Frames it as both a leadership transition and an ongoing corruption probe. Contains a lengthy author bio unrelated to the story.
framing_analysis.The Weekly Times: Headline-only in this dossier (no retrievable body text). Headline frames it narrowly as 'Paraguayan Congress Announces Impeachment' — notably lags the others by stopping at the announcement rather than the completed removal and arrest. No body to assess.

primary_source_alignment: No primary sources (roll-call vote record, impeachment writ, prosecutor filings, or central bank resolution order) were located for this story, so no document-level verification of the vote count, charges, or financial figures is possible.
Key contested figures — the exact Senate tally (44 of 45 vs. all 44 present) and the pension deposit amount ($355m vs. $380m) — cannot be adjudicated against an underlying record in this dossier.
missing_context: No outlet explains the constitutional/legal basis for arresting a sitting president at the moment of impeachment, nor the procedural standard used (BBC notes impeachment strips ex-president immunity but the mechanics are unexplained).
No primary source (vote record, impeachment charges, prosecutor filing) was available, so the brief relies entirely on outlet reporting for contested numbers.

Only three of seven dossier articles (BBC twice, Al Jazeera, Hindustan Times — effectively three distinct outlets) have substantive body text; Reuters, The Times of India, and The Weekly Times are headline-only, limiting corroboration.
No outlet details who audited or first corrected Ueno's books, or when regulators first received warnings about insider lending versus when they acted.
Little coverage of opposition versus Colorado Party dynamics beyond the vote — the question of why Peña's own party voted to remove him is noted but not explained.
No outlet reports international reaction (IMF, regional governments, markets) despite Peña's IMF background and the scale of the financial collapse.
The fate and legal status of ex-central bank chief Carvallo (ordered arrested per Hindustan Times) is left unresolved — 'not immediately clear whether Carvallo had been taken into custody.'
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Three full-text outlets (BBC, Al Jazeera, Hindustan Times) reported the same event with materially different emphases — dramatic democratic moment, systemic banking-crisis explainer, and succession/prosecution procedural — while key figures (vote tally, pension deposit) diverge and no primary source exists to adjudicate, making this a coverage-comparison story rather than a straight REPORT.
